blocks.text: Finding 1 (ADOPT, p2) — Flat top-level supervision tree shares one restart budget

content.value: Filed: task-d328fb91ff55b743 (parent task-9e2fc23e66db1de5, priority 2, labels felix/phoenix-audit-finding).

Barkpark.Application starts ~30 children under ONE flat supervisor with NO restart-intensity override, so OTP's default 3-restarts-in-5s applies to the ENTIRE tree at once. Plugin-contributed workers fold in FLAT next to Repo, Oban, PubSub and Endpoint. There are no intermediate supervisors (grep confirms only Telemetry has its own; the Sheets/StudioChat DynamicSupervisors hold restart:temporary children that don't count against the top budget).

blocks.value:
opts = [strategy: :one_for_one, name: Barkpark.Supervisor]  # application.ex:185 — no max_restarts/max_seconds
children = [RateLimiter, Telemetry, RequestStats, Repo, Vault, Plugins.Registry, ...]
           ++ plugin_children   # Pulse.Metrics, Quiz.Bridge, Github.Auth+DrainWorker, OnixEdit — FLAT
           ++ [SchemaBootstrap, Indx.Auth, Indx.Monitor, Indx.Recovery, {Oban,...},
               PubSub, Sheets registries+supervisors, StudioChat registries+supervisors,
               Presence, TaskSupervisors, ...SelfUpdate.Runner, Endpoint]

content.value: NAMED FAILURE MODE — concrete inputs to wrong outcome: any ONE top-level child that crash-loops (raises in init/handle_continue 3x within 5s — e.g. a future or third-party plugin worker validating external config at boot, or several DB-touching workers each crashing ONCE inside the same 5s window during a Postgres blip) breaches Barkpark.Supervisor's SHARED 3/5s intensity. The top supervisor then terminates ALL siblings — Repo, Oban and Endpoint included — so a contained subsystem fault escalates to a TOTAL application outage (every request 502s) instead of degrading.

The sharp irony: the code already invests in graceful degradation at the QUERY layer — engine=indx is designed to 'silently fall back to Postgres' when Indx is unreachable (application.ex:112-119). But a crash-LOOPING Indx or plugin process would take the whole box down at the SUPERVISION layer before that fallback ever runs. Chapter 64 doctrine: 'Layering isolates blast radius'; 'Flat supervision trees' is the named anti-pattern.

HONEST SCOPING: today's children are individually hardened (Indx.Recovery wraps its pass in try/rescue; the Auth caches are lazy), so the fault is LATENT, not currently reachable. This qualifies under doctrine #4 (provably-cheaper future change): grouping the volatile plugin/subsystem tiers under intermediate supervisors with their own restart intensity contains any subtree crash-loop structurally, so adding a fallible worker no longer risks a whole-app shutdown and authors stop re-implementing crash isolation per worker.

PROTECTIVE MEASUREMENT (delegated to the fix task): build a replica supervisor with the same flat shape + default intensity containing a deliberately crash-looping child; assert the WHOLE supervisor terminates (escalation reproduced). After the fix the same crash-looper tears down only its own subtree while Repo/Endpoint-equivalent siblings stay up. Fix must preserve boot ORDER (Auth->Recovery->Oban, host services before Endpoint) and the default-off/fresh-install invariants.

blocks.text: Validation singletons — GenServer.call on a 'hot' path

content.value: Content.Validation.Rules.for_schema/1 and Validation.Registry.find/1 look like a per-mutate singleton serialization point. But Evaluator.run/3 — the only caller of for_schema/1 — has ZERO non-test callers in lib/ (cross-field validation is not yet wired into any mutate/export path; WI2 not landed). Validation.Registry.find/1 already reads ETS directly (no GenServer round-trip), and Rules explicitly documents the map-over-ETS tradeoff. No live hot path exists, so converting to persistent_term now would be premature optimization of unexercised code (Chapter 5 anti-pattern). Reject; revisit when WI2 wires the evaluator in.

blocks.text: Auth token caches block HTTP inside handle_call

content.value: Github.Auth, Bokbasen.Auth and Indx.Auth all run a synchronous ~30s Req token exchange inside handle_call(:token). The blocking window head-of-line-blocks other :token/:invalidate callers. Rejected: the serialization IS the intended in-flight de-dup (documented), the token is cached ~1h so a fetch is rare, and all three plugins are off-by-default. No measured cost; the async-reply refactor adds complexity for a pathological-only (upstream-hang) benefit.

RateLimiter, RequestStats and Plugins.Registry were checked for a sharding win. RateLimiter uses one public ETS table with write_concurrency (distinct keys don't contend; same-key contention is inherent to a per-client bucket). RequestStats inserts unique {time,uniq} keys with write_concurrency. Plugins.Registry serves hot lookups from a persistent_term snapshot. Sheets.Session and Quiz.Room are ALREADY Registry-sharded per entity. No measured bottleneck anywhere — Chapter 5/65 'measure before over-engineering' says reject.
RateLimiter — ETS public token bucket, read/write_concurrency, opportunistic bounded prune at 10k entries (Chapter 68 compliant: rate limiting in ETS, not a GenServer).
RequestStats — ETS write path from the telemetry handler (never serializes through the mailbox), rare GenServer read, timer-pruned to ~one window; honest null p95 on empty window.

Sheets.Session fleet — lazy per-sheet GenServer, Registry-keyed under a DynamicSupervisor, restart:temporary (reloads from persisted row), hibernate_after wired (session.ex:402), idle-stop, 30s shutdown to persist the tail. Mailbox is the serializer but sync apply_ops calls backpressure callers and a 1000-op-per-call cap bounds a single batch. The brief's hibernation ask is already satisfied.

Pulse.Metrics — exemplary: hot-path bumps via lock-free :counters fetched through :persistent_term (no-op with the plugin off), a 2s self-tick sampler, snapshot reads from :persistent_term so a busy dashboard cannot back-pressure the sampler.

Plugins.Registry — hot lookups (all/0, collect_*) read a :persistent_term snapshot; the GenServer.call is a cold fallback only. Correct Chapter 5 use of persistent_term for a read-mostly, rarely-written registry.

ETS growth — all 8 tables bounded: RateLimiter, RequestStats, Indx.Monitor, search SurfaceConfigs and the DEK cache use the clear-on-full pattern (#790/#792); codelists' alias cache is keyed by plugin name (fixed small cardinality). No unbounded-growth vein.

DrainWorker — level-triggered self-tick poll loop with a reentrancy guard, capped backoff, and a memoized active-gate; never receives hot-path messages, so no mailbox blowup. Indx.Recovery/Auth are crash-loop-hardened (try/rescue pass; lazy init). self_update.Checker fetches asynchronously (spawns, replies via handle_info) rather than blocking.

Startup ordering — the flat list encodes real dependencies by position with explaining comments (Repo/Vault/Registry before plugin workers; SchemaBootstrap synchronously before Oban so no job dequeues against an unregistered schema; Auth->Recovery->Oban; host services before Endpoint). This is a deliberately-ordered flat tree, not a naive one — the ONLY topology gap is blast-radius layering (Finding 1).

Sheets.Session mailbox blowup under load          already-good        Registry-sharded, sync-call backpressure, 1000-op cap
Pulse.Metrics (live cost telemetry)               already-good        metrics.ex :counters + :persistent_term, no hot mailbox
Plugins.Registry hot-path lookups                 already-good        registry.ex:114 persistent_term snapshot fast-path
Validation.Registry / Content.Validation.Rules    rejected-w-reason   evaluator.run has ZERO non-test callers (dormant)
  singleton GenServer.call on 'hot' path
Github/Bokbasen/Indx Auth: HTTP in handle_call    rejected-w-reason   ~1h cache, off-by-default, de-dup is intended
ETS unbounded growth (all 8 tables)               already-good        clear-on-full pattern #790/#792; codelists=plugin-keyed
PartitionSupervisor opportunity (RateLimiter/     rejected-w-reason   no measured bottleneck; write_concurrency suffices
  RequestStats/Registry)                                              (Chapter 5: no premature ETS/sharding)
Indx.Recovery / Auth crash-loop hardening         already-good        recovery.ex try/rescue; auth.ex lazy init

Finding 1 (ADOPT, p2) — Flat top-level supervision tree shares one restart budget

Filed: task-d328fb91ff55b743 (parent task-9e2fc23e66db1de5, priority 2, labels felix/phoenix-audit-finding).

Barkpark.Application starts ~30 children under ONE flat supervisor with NO restart-intensity override, so OTP's default 3-restarts-in-5s applies to the ENTIRE tree at once. Plugin-contributed workers fold in FLAT next to Repo, Oban, PubSub and Endpoint. There are no intermediate supervisors (grep confirms only Telemetry has its own; the Sheets/StudioChat DynamicSupervisors hold restart:temporary children that don't count against the top budget).

opts = [strategy: :one_for_one, name: Barkpark.Supervisor]  # application.ex:185 — no max_restarts/max_seconds
children = [RateLimiter, Telemetry, RequestStats, Repo, Vault, Plugins.Registry, ...]
           ++ plugin_children   # Pulse.Metrics, Quiz.Bridge, Github.Auth+DrainWorker, OnixEdit — FLAT
           ++ [SchemaBootstrap, Indx.Auth, Indx.Monitor, Indx.Recovery, {Oban,...},
               PubSub, Sheets registries+supervisors, StudioChat registries+supervisors,
               Presence, TaskSupervisors, ...SelfUpdate.Runner, Endpoint]

NAMED FAILURE MODE — concrete inputs to wrong outcome: any ONE top-level child that crash-loops (raises in init/handle_continue 3x within 5s — e.g. a future or third-party plugin worker validating external config at boot, or several DB-touching workers each crashing ONCE inside the same 5s window during a Postgres blip) breaches Barkpark.Supervisor's SHARED 3/5s intensity. The top supervisor then terminates ALL siblings — Repo, Oban and Endpoint included — so a contained subsystem fault escalates to a TOTAL application outage (every request 502s) instead of degrading.

The sharp irony: the code already invests in graceful degradation at the QUERY layer — engine=indx is designed to 'silently fall back to Postgres' when Indx is unreachable (application.ex:112-119). But a crash-LOOPING Indx or plugin process would take the whole box down at the SUPERVISION layer before that fallback ever runs. Chapter 64 doctrine: 'Layering isolates blast radius'; 'Flat supervision trees' is the named anti-pattern.

HONEST SCOPING: today's children are individually hardened (Indx.Recovery wraps its pass in try/rescue; the Auth caches are lazy), so the fault is LATENT, not currently reachable. This qualifies under doctrine #4 (provably-cheaper future change): grouping the volatile plugin/subsystem tiers under intermediate supervisors with their own restart intensity contains any subtree crash-loop structurally, so adding a fallible worker no longer risks a whole-app shutdown and authors stop re-implementing crash isolation per worker.

PROTECTIVE MEASUREMENT (delegated to the fix task): build a replica supervisor with the same flat shape + default intensity containing a deliberately crash-looping child; assert the WHOLE supervisor terminates (escalation reproduced). After the fix the same crash-looper tears down only its own subtree while Repo/Endpoint-equivalent siblings stay up. Fix must preserve boot ORDER (Auth->Recovery->Oban, host services before Endpoint) and the default-off/fresh-install invariants.

Rejected-with-reason (first-class verdicts)

Validation singletons — GenServer.call on a 'hot' path

Content.Validation.Rules.for_schema/1 and Validation.Registry.find/1 look like a per-mutate singleton serialization point. But Evaluator.run/3 — the only caller of for_schema/1 — has ZERO non-test callers in lib/ (cross-field validation is not yet wired into any mutate/export path; WI2 not landed). Validation.Registry.find/1 already reads ETS directly (no GenServer round-trip), and Rules explicitly documents the map-over-ETS tradeoff. No live hot path exists, so converting to persistent_term now would be premature optimization of unexercised code (Chapter 5 anti-pattern). Reject; revisit when WI2 wires the evaluator in.

Auth token caches block HTTP inside handle_call

Github.Auth, Bokbasen.Auth and Indx.Auth all run a synchronous ~30s Req token exchange inside handle_call(:token). The blocking window head-of-line-blocks other :token/:invalidate callers. Rejected: the serialization IS the intended in-flight de-dup (documented), the token is cached ~1h so a fetch is rare, and all three plugins are off-by-default. No measured cost; the async-reply refactor adds complexity for a pathological-only (upstream-hang) benefit.

PartitionSupervisor / sharding opportunities

RateLimiter, RequestStats and Plugins.Registry were checked for a sharding win. RateLimiter uses one public ETS table with write_concurrency (distinct keys don't contend; same-key contention is inherent to a per-client bucket). RequestStats inserts unique {time,uniq} keys with write_concurrency. Plugins.Registry serves hot lookups from a persistent_term snapshot. Sheets.Session and Quiz.Room are ALREADY Registry-sharded per entity. No measured bottleneck anywhere — Chapter 5/65 'measure before over-engineering' says reject.

Already-good (verified, no change)

RateLimiter — ETS public token bucket, read/write_concurrency, opportunistic bounded prune at 10k entries (Chapter 68 compliant: rate limiting in ETS, not a GenServer).

RequestStats — ETS write path from the telemetry handler (never serializes through the mailbox), rare GenServer read, timer-pruned to ~one window; honest null p95 on empty window.

Sheets.Session fleet — lazy per-sheet GenServer, Registry-keyed under a DynamicSupervisor, restart:temporary (reloads from persisted row), hibernate_after wired (session.ex:402), idle-stop, 30s shutdown to persist the tail. Mailbox is the serializer but sync apply_ops calls backpressure callers and a 1000-op-per-call cap bounds a single batch. The brief's hibernation ask is already satisfied.

Pulse.Metrics — exemplary: hot-path bumps via lock-free :counters fetched through :persistent_term (no-op with the plugin off), a 2s self-tick sampler, snapshot reads from :persistent_term so a busy dashboard cannot back-pressure the sampler.

Plugins.Registry — hot lookups (all/0, collect_*) read a :persistent_term snapshot; the GenServer.call is a cold fallback only. Correct Chapter 5 use of persistent_term for a read-mostly, rarely-written registry.

ETS growth — all 8 tables bounded: RateLimiter, RequestStats, Indx.Monitor, search SurfaceConfigs and the DEK cache use the clear-on-full pattern (#790/#792); codelists' alias cache is keyed by plugin name (fixed small cardinality). No unbounded-growth vein.

DrainWorker — level-triggered self-tick poll loop with a reentrancy guard, capped backoff, and a memoized active-gate; never receives hot-path messages, so no mailbox blowup. Indx.Recovery/Auth are crash-loop-hardened (try/rescue pass; lazy init). self_update.Checker fetches asynchronously (spawns, replies via handle_info) rather than blocking.

Startup ordering — the flat list encodes real dependencies by position with explaining comments (Repo/Vault/Registry before plugin workers; SchemaBootstrap synchronously before Oban so no job dequeues against an unregistered schema; Auth->Recovery->Oban; host services before Endpoint). This is a deliberately-ordered flat tree, not a naive one — the ONLY topology gap is blast-radius layering (Finding 1).
